research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10901 (Federal Register of January 12, 1961, 26 FR 217; govinfo text layer, recorded as acceptable as original, grade original_representation_unverified). The held text is headed Executive Order 10901, Amendment of Executive Order No. 10501, Relating to Safeguarding Official Information in the Interests of the Defense of the United States; it is signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower at the White House on January 9, 1961 and carries the filing line Filed, Jan. 11, 1961. Text and inventory: section 1 substitutes a new section 2 of Executive Order 10501 (limitation of authority to classify), consisting of an introductory paragraph and subsections (a) (agencies with primary national-defense responsibility, which may delegate classification authority), (b) (agencies with partial responsibility, authority exercised only by the agency head) and (c) (unnamed or future agencies have no classification authority unless conferred). Section 2 revokes the President's memoranda of November 5, 1953, May 7, 1959 and March 9, 1960. The registered inventory split section 1 at a stray page-footnote fragment (labels sec1 and sec1-7049) and omitted section 2, so I replaced it with two clauses, section 1 and section 2. Ending: Executive Order 11652 of March 8, 1972 (37 FR 5209), section 14, states that Executive Order 10501 of November 5, 1953, as amended by Executive Orders 10816, 10901, 10964, 10985, 11097 and by section 1(a) of 11382, is superseded as of the effective date of that order, and section 15 states that it becomes effective on June 1, 1972. Because Executive Order 10901's substituted section 2 is the text of Executive Order 10501 that was amended, that supersession ends the section 1 clause on 1972-06-01. The section 2 revocation of three memoranda was a one-time act performed when the order took effect and is dated 1961-01-09. Status and searches: the status history holds two editorial leads that I did not rely on. The three machine searches were read; current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr showed no operative citation of this order, and later-events:ofr_catalog shows the 1972 supersession. Executive Orders 10964, 10985, 11097 and 11382 later amended Executive Order 10501 (the three last ones the lists in section 2) and are recorded as later events; Executive Order 11171 of 1964 states it does not modify or supersede Executive Order 10501.
savings_reason: Executive Order 11652 section 14 contains no saving clause for the superseded section 2; the transitional provisions of Executive Order 11652 deal with information classified under Executive Order 10501, which is a consequence of classifications made under the earlier order, not a continuing command of Executive Order 10901. I found no held source showing a surviving appointment, transfer or right created by this order itself.
earlier_end_check: I searched the held corpus for the number 10901 and for the parent order. Executive Orders 10985, 11097 and 11382 amend the lists in section 2 of Executive Order 10501 by adding or deleting agencies and Executive Order 10964 amends other sections; none replaces section 2 as a whole or revokes it, so the substituted text remained in force as amended until the 1972 supersession. Executive Order 11171 expressly does not modify or supersede Executive Order 10501. No earlier end of section 1 is shown; the one-time revocation in section 2 is dated separately.

The 'target provision not located' notes in the dossier concern the machine matching of Executive Orders 10985, 11097 and 11652; I read each of those texts and confirmed the provisions above.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10994 at 27 FR 1447 (Federal Register of Friday, February 16, 1962, PDF pages 3-6; govinfo text layer, recorded as acceptable as original, grade original_representation_unverified). The held text is headed Executive Order 10994, The President's Committee on Employment of the Handicapped, is signed by John F. Kennedy at the White House in February 1962 and carries the filing line Filed, Feb. 14, 1962. Text and inventory: I read the whole order. Its authority recital cites the Joint Resolution of July 11, 1949 (63 Stat. 409) and section 8 of the Vocational Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 38). Section 1 establishes the President's Committee and sets its composition, member terms and invitations; section 2 states its functions; section 3 establishes the Executive Committee; section 4 establishes the Advisory Council; section 5 deals with meetings, acting officers, rules, compensation, employees and Department of Labor support; section 6(a) says the order controls over inconsistent prior measures and supersedes Executive Order 10640; section 6(b) moves the members, employees, records, property, funds and business of the predecessor committee to the new committee on the date of the order; section 6(c) fixes the tenure of those transferred members. The registered inventory was wrong: it omitted section 1(a), section 2, section 3(a), section 5(a) and section 6(a), and mislabelled other pieces (labels such as sec4-b and b-dup2 actually cover parts of sections 3, 5 and 6). I replaced it with nine clauses that cover the order from section 1 through section 6(c) without overlap (the authority recital and title are not operative commands). Ending: Executive Order 11480 of September 9, 1969 (34 FR 14273), section 6(a), states that Executive Order 10994 of February 14, 1962 and Executive Order 11018 of April 27, 1962 are hereby superseded. The supersession names this order, has no exception and re-creates the Committee under the new order, so it reaches every clause. Executive Order 11018 of April 27, 1962 earlier amended only the first sentence of section 1(b), raising the number of Vice Chairmen from three to four; that is a later amendment event, not an end. Status and searches: the status history holds two editorial leads (upper bound 1989-01-20) that I did not rely on. The three machine searches were read: current-law:usc found one codification note (29 U.S.C. 791, which cites this order as amended) that reflects the history, current-law:ecfr found nothing operative, and later-events:ofr_catalog shows the supersession. No held instrument revives the order after 1969.
savings_reason: Executive Order 11480 section 6(b) provides that all members, employees, records, property, funds and pending business of the Committee provided for in Executive Order 10994, as amended, become those of the Committee established by Executive Order 11480, and section 6(c) continues member tenure. This is a transfer of accrued members and business to the successor committee, not a continuing command of Executive Order 10994, so the savings state is transferred_or_accrued. No held source shows any other surviving right.
earlier_end_check: I searched the held corpus for the number 10994. The only instruments naming it are Executive Order 11018 (amends section 1(b) only), Executive Order 11480 (supersedes it) and the codification note in 29 U.S.C. 791. The 1989 and API disposition notes give only an upper bound. No instrument before Executive Order 11480 revokes or supersedes any part of the order, so the first end of the committee clauses is 1969-09-09. Two clauses ended earlier by their own terms and are dated separately: the supersession of Executive Order 10640 in section 6(a) took effect when this order took effect, and the transfer in section 6(b) is stated to occur on the date of the order.
scope_check: Executive Order 11480 section 6(a) supersedes Executive Order 10994 by number and without exception, so it reaches all committee clauses. Executive Order 11018 amends only the first sentence of section 1(b); the rest of section 1(b) and every other clause are unaffected until 1969. The members' tenure in section 6(c) has two limbs (presidential appointees at the pleasure of the President; others for their unexpired terms under Executive Order 10640); the held sources do not date when the unexpired terms ran out, but the pleasure limb and the rest of the order stayed in force until 1969-09-09, which is the date I record for that clause as a whole.
independent_command_check: The standing commands (the Committee, Executive Committee and Advisory Council, their functions and administration) all depend on the same bodies and end together with the order. The two transitional commands (supersession of Executive Order 10640 and the transfer of members, records and funds) are one-time acts completed when the order took effect and are dated separately; they do not run on to 1969.

This is a transfer of accrued members and business to the successor committee, not a continuing command of Executive Order 10994, so the savings state is transferred_or_accrued. research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11218 at 30 FR 5821 (Federal Register of Tuesday, April 27, 1965, PDF page 9; govinfo text layer, recorded as acceptable as original, grade original_representation_unverified). The held text is headed Executive Order 11218, Amending Executive Order No. 11017 so as to make the Chairman of the Tennessee Valley Authority a member of the Recreation Advisory Council; it is signed by Lyndon B. Johnson at the White House in April 1965, and its filing line reads Filed, Apr. 26, 1965. Text: it is a single paragraph that further amends Executive Order No. 11017 of April 27, 1962, as amended, by substituting for subsection (a) of Section 1 a new text that establishes the Recreation Advisory Council and lists its members, adding the Chairman of the Tennessee Valley Authority, and that sets a two-year rotating chairmanship and a rule for inviting heads of non-member agencies. The clause inventory has one clause, the whole paragraph, and I confirm it is complete. Ending: Executive Order 11278 of May 4, 1966 (31 FR 6681, held in the Federal Register text and in the American Presidency Project mirror) states in its section 106, headed Prior orders, that Executive Orders 11017, 11069 and 11218 are hereby superseded. That section names this order by number, carries no exception or delayed date, and the order replaces the Recreation Advisory Council with the President's Council on Recreation and Natural Beauty (Part I), so the supersession reaches the whole of this order. The OCR of the Federal Register copy reads 'bf' for 'of' before the date of Executive Order 11218; the American Presidency Project mirror reads it correctly, and the number and date identify this order. Status: the status history is not empty but holds only two editorial leads; the status rests on the held text of Executive Order 11278. Any current-law need does not arise for a NO. A bounded search of the three machine searches (current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr, no hits for this order; later-events:ofr_catalog, one hit, the supersession by Executive Order 11278) shows no instrument that revives or continues the order.
savings_reason: Executive Order 11278 contains no saving clause for this order. Its section 101(b) provides that prior service as chairman of the Recreation Advisory Council under Executive Order 11017, as amended, counts as service as chairman of the new Council for purposes of rotation; this is a carried-over accrued service credit, not a continuing command of Executive Order 11218, so the savings state is transferred_or_accrued. Nothing in the held sources shows a surviving appointment or right created by this order itself, which only changed the list of members.
earlier_end_check: I searched the held corpus for the numbers of this order and of its parent. Executive Order 11017 is cited by Executive Orders 11069, 11200, 11218, 11237 and 11278; none of them revokes or supersedes this order or the parent before Executive Order 11278 (Executive Order 11069 amends the same subsection earlier, in 1962, and Executive Order 11200 and 11237 only cite the Council). This order was never amended or superseded by any held instrument before 1966-05-04, so no earlier end is shown and none is claimed.
scope_check: Section 106 of Executive Order 11278 lists this order by number among the orders superseded and the enacting words have no exception, so it reaches the whole of the single clause. The order is an amendment of subsection (a) of section 1 of Executive Order 11017, and the amended parent is superseded in the same sentence, so no part survives as a free-standing command.
independent_command_check: The order has one command, the substituted text of subsection (a) of section 1 of Executive Order 11017. It states no separate duty, deadline or term that could survive independently of the Council it describes; the superseding order creates a differently named council (the President's Council on Recreation and Natural Beauty) with its own membership.
